correctness.rationale: The proof was reconstructed at the level of a single decoding functional. From any infinite subset of the pullback code it first recovers the uniformly introreducible core, then an infinite subset of a finite-initial-segment code, then the coded real and the full pullback. Both Turing-degree inequalities and the lower-cone obstruction were checked separately.

originality.rationale: The ownership source proves existence of a uniformly introreducible core, while the closest located cone theorem of Kumar and Shelah is only for introreducible subsets. Targeted searches found no equivalent uniform cone or common-decoder statement. The inaccessible full text of the 1968 foundational article leaves a documented residual priority risk but no affirmative overlap evidence.

value.rationale: The result converts existence of one uniformly introreducible subset into an exact upper-cone spectrum inside a selected core and supplies one decoder for a family realizing every degree in that cone, providing substantive hereditary degree control.
